baseline_stage_from: dev (same pinned base digest as the measurement toolchain) + gzip/zstd/xz/brotli/jq/pv/time/strace + tabix(bgzip)/pixz + perl 5.36
commands: docker compose build baseline   # adds tabix(bgzip) + pixz to the dev-derived stage

docker compose run --rm --no-TTY baseline sh tools/seekable-baselines.sh evidence/scratch/phase8/seekable.jsonl evidence/corpus/phase8-large/large.pdf evidence/scratch/phase8/large.seek.voldoc evidence/scratch/phase8/sb
method: For each pre-registered byte range the seekable baseline court builds the archive, locates the compressed block(s) that cover the range from the format's own index (`tools/bgzf-seek-probe.pl` reads the `.gzi` index plus the BGZF block map via each block's gzip ISIZE trailer; `tools/xz-seek-probe.pl` reads the xz Stream Footer and Index field), and counts bytes-read as the covering compressed block(s) + the index/framing that locates them. xz and pixz covering blocks are decoded *in isolation* (`tools/xz-block-reframe.pl` rebuilds a minimal single-stream `.xz` of exactly those blocks, proving the `--block-size` blocks are independently decodable); BGZF covering blocks are decoded as lone gzip members. Every extracted slice is `cmp`-identical to the source range. The VOLE row is the seeked `view`'s instrumented `bytes_read` on the same range. Archives built here: `bgzip -l 9` (7,995,600 B), `xz --block-size=64KiB` (6,393,552 B), `1MiB` (5,797,248 B), `4MiB` (5,725,576 B), `pixz` (5,689,264 B); VOLE seekable descriptor 17,566,832 B; source 33,789,340 B.
caveats: This is the honest random-access comparison: against *seekable/blocked* formats VOLE does NOT win generally. For the late query (a=32,505,856) VOLE reads 460,713 B versus bgzip 23,808 B (~19x fewer), xz --block-size=64KiB 15,344 B (~30x fewer) and 1MiB 179,892 B (~2.6x fewer); it reads *more* than xz --block-size=4MiB (708,612 B) and pixz (2,810,832 B, whose default 16 MiB blocks make a byte-range seek expensive). The Phase-8.3 claim is therefore restated: the win is over *non-seekable sequential* gzip/zstd/xz prefixes only. `pixz --seekable` does not exist; `zstd` 1.5.4 has no seekable mode. Costs model what a random-access reader must read (covering blocks + index); they are not sequential prefix reads. Single locally generated corpus; no population claim.
